title: KYA-OS conformance attestation credential (v1)
description: A W3C VC 2.0 credential asserting one observed conformance test result: the named implementation, at the pinned code digest, passed the pinned suite. Deliberately no validUntil (additionalProperties: false forbids it): currency is judged against the published suite manifest, so supersession of the suite, not the passage of time, is what dates a credential. Structural validation in this repo is enforced by scripts/lib/shape.mjs - keep that module and this schema in sync.
$comment: Version 1 changed in place in November 2026 (issue #52): proof.@context became required, proof.created took the dateTimeStamp grammar (proof.$comment says how), and validFrom's pattern became the program timestamp's lexical grammar, which refuses a month, day, hour, minute or second out of range, such as 2026-13-01T00:00:00Z, that the earlier pattern let through. A credential valid under the earlier text fails this one, and the reverse. The schema keeps its id, which every issued credential signs as its credentialSchema.id; each of those gained proof.@context with its signature unchanged.

id.description: Deterministic id: urn:kya:conf: plus the first 32 hex of SHA-256 over 'kya-conf-id-v1' NUL subjectId NUL suiteVersion NUL vectorSetHash NUL level NUL scope NUL hex(sha256(JCS(categories or []))). Same claim inputs always yield the same id.

validFrom.description: Issuance instant, in the program's timestamp form: an XMLSCHEMA11-2 dateTimeStamp in UTC to the second, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ. The pattern is its lexical grammar; the verifiers also refuse a day its month does not have, and a validFrom 300 seconds or more in the future. There is deliberately no validUntil property anywhere in this schema.

id.description: The subject's canonical identifier: an https URL or a DID.

gitCommit.description: The exact commit the program re-ran. The credential attests this code state, not a moving branch.

categories.description: Vector categories the claim covers, sorted lexicographically. Required when scope is subset; forbidden when scope is full. A subset never renders as a bare level.

credentialStatus.description: Exactly two BitstringStatusListEntry objects, revocation then suspension, sharing one allocated index (the allocation ledger lives at registry/credentials/allocations.json).

proof.$comment: proof.@context became required in November 2026 (issue #52), changing this schema in place: VC Data Integrity EdDSA Cryptosuites v1.0, section 3.3.1 step 2, has the signer store the document's @context in the proof, so that a verifier rebuilds the signed proof configuration from the stored proof alone (section 3.3.2). Credentials committed before then gained the property with their signatures unchanged, because the signer had always signed over it. The same change replaced proof.created's UTC-only pattern with the dateTimeStamp lexical grammar, which differs both ways: it admits an offset, fractional seconds, and a negative year or one of more than four digits, which the old pattern refused, and refuses a month, day, hour, minute or second out of range, such as 2026-13-01T00:00:00Z or 2016-12-31T23:59:60Z, which the old pattern let through; every committed credential's created satisfies both.

created.description: An XMLSCHEMA11-2 dateTimeStamp, as VC Data Integrity 1.0 section 2.1 requires: a datetime with its timezone, Z or an offset. The pattern is its lexical grammar; the day-of-month constraint XMLSCHEMA11-2 section 3.3.7.2 attaches to that grammar is checked by the verifiers, which refuse a day its month does not have, such as February 29 outside a leap year.

@context.description: The credential's own @context, stored in the proof as VC Data Integrity EdDSA Cryptosuites v1.0 section 3.3.1 step 2 requires, so a verifier rebuilds the signed proof configuration from the stored proof alone (section 3.3.2).
